author: Cypra Probatii; ed. Marcin 'MKG' Gerkowicz
title: Death of the Governor
forces: Defender 1000 points plus planetary installations (governor's palace, airfield, laser battery, missile battery). Attacker 500 points.
summary: A small fast force must land strike squads on the Governor's palace. The attack is a hit-and-run on the palace (0 hits, no shields, 2 turrets, cannot be destroyed) that succeeds on a 4+. The defender wins if the Governor lives at the end of turn 6 or the attacker is destroyed or disengaged.
special_rules: D3 defending units on full alert, the rest on standby in orbit
Attackers enter from any edge(s) in turn 1
Hit-and-run on the palace succeeds on 4+
xr_dependencies: Scenarios: Surprise Attack (full alert and standby)

xr_conflicts.source_text: This attack is succesfull on a D6 roll of a 4+ (the Governor is well guarded).
xr_conflicts.xr_text: Against small units which do not use the Critical Hits table, a hit-and-run attack causes one point of damage on a D6 roll of 4+
xr_conflicts.effect: Compatible in odds. XR raids are made by assault boats, boarding torpedoes and teleports against ships; the source says the raid is 'a hit-and-run attack' without naming the craft or saying the palace's 2 turrets apply to the raiders (XR s.31 step 1).

xr_conflicts.source_text: D3 Defending ships/squadrons are on full alert, and placed anythere on the table no closer than 20cm to table edge. The rest of the Defending forces are on standby in orbit.
xr_conflicts.xr_text: the defender must choose D3 ships or squadrons in their fleet to be on full alert. These ships may be deployed anywhere on the table at least 30cm from a table edge.
xr_conflicts.effect: Same mechanism with 20cm instead of 30cm; no standby wake-up test is given in the source.

xr_conflicts: Checked: attack rating not used; no special orders restrictions; terrain by standard generator (s.39).
missing_or_unclear: Profiles of the airfield, laser battery and missile battery (not in the book's defences pages or in Support Assets).
How the 'Governor's palace' is targeted from space and whether the palace needs to be inside low orbit range.
How standby units become active.
Table size ('a square 120-140cm long table').
Whether the low orbit table is used for the hit-and-run (the source asks for one).
notes: Gehenna campaign special scenario. Needs the Book of Nemesis campaign (tree campaign, pp.36-39) and its defence profiles (pp.24-27). Effect on campaign: D3 random units gain or lose 1 Ld.

author: Cypra Probatii; ed. Marcin 'MKG' Gerkowicz
title: Guns of Naravona
forces: 1000 points each. The Defender also has the Naravona Battlestation (250pts) in the middle of the defender's deployment zone.
summary: The attacker must destroy the Naravona Battlestation, which guards a passage; no terrain in the middle of the table. On a 4+ the attacker deploys one of the defender's ships or squadrons.
special_rules: Naravona Passage terrain restriction
Attacker may deploy defender units on a 4+
xr_dependencies: Book of Nemesis defences (Naravona class battlestation p.25)

xr_conflicts.source_text: The controlling fleet, until the end of the campaign, may re-roll failed Reload Ordnance tests once per battle.
xr_conflicts.xr_section: s.7 Special Orders; s.5 Fleet Commanders
xr_conflicts.xr_text: Reload Ordnance: If the ship passes its command check, all of its ordnance is successfully reloaded
xr_conflicts.effect: A campaign benefit that adds a free re-roll outside fleet commander re-rolls (s.5).

xr_conflicts: Checked: standard deployment, VP and game length (until Naravona destroyed or fleet destroyed/disengaged). No attack rating roll.
missing_or_unclear: Who is the attacker (not stated; the campaign decides).
Naravona's profile and Van Holderman cannon (nova cannon rules): the book gives them on pp.25-26.
Whether the attacker deploying a defender ship counts against either fleet's points.
Table size and which edges.
notes: Gehenna campaign special scenario. Needs the Book of Nemesis campaign (tree campaign, pp.36-39) and its defence profiles (pp.24-27).

author: Cypra Probatii; ed. Marcin 'MKG' Gerkowicz
title: Shadow of the Comet
forces: 500 points each. Defender also has an Orbital Command Center, 2 Orbital Weapon Platforms, 1 Orbital Flak Platform and 2 Orbital Torpedo Launchers in high orbit round the second moon.
summary: The attackers use a comet as cover to approach a Mechanicus base. While every attacking ship is within 10cm of the comet and has not opened fire or gone on special orders, the defenders cannot attack them. Detection on a D6 of 6 (+1 if a defender is within 10cm of an attacker) at the start of each defender turn. The attacker wins by boarding the Orbital Command Center and disengaging one ship.
special_rules: Comet cover (stealth)
Detection roll each defender turn
Defenders on patrol until detected; attacker moves defenders on a 4+ in movement
xr_dependencies: Support Assets: Orbital Weapons Platform, Orbital Torpedo Launcher

xr_conflicts.source_text: an Orbital Command Center, 2 Orbital Weapon Platforms, 1 Orbital Flak Platform and 2 Orbital Torpedo Launchers
xr_conflicts.xr_text: Orbital Weapons Platform Defence | 30 | 2 | ... Macrobatteries 60cm FP6 (All Round) | Immobile
xr_conflicts.effect: The weapons platform and torpedo launcher exist in Support Assets with their own profiles; the Command Center and Flak platform are Book of Nemesis profiles (p.26) and are not in the booklet.

xr_conflicts.source_text: Roll a D6 in the movement phase for each ship/squadron - on a 4+ the attacker may move the Defender's ship or squadron.
xr_conflicts.xr_text: During his or her turn, a player can move and fight with all of his or her ships.
xr_conflicts.effect: The attacker moves enemy patrol ships; the source gives no limits (speed, turns).

xr_conflicts: Checked: boarding (s.32) is used by the attacker to win; standard deployment with the 4+ attacker-deploys-defender option as in Naravona.
missing_or_unclear: Comet 'cover' radius beyond 10cm and its movement.
Whether the comet is a phenomenon with its own effects (rules 'path of the comet').
Orbital Command Center troop rating.
'Disengage at least one of his ships': any disengage route.
notes: Gehenna campaign special scenario. Needs the Book of Nemesis campaign (tree campaign, pp.36-39) and its defence profiles (pp.24-27). Effect on campaign: D3 refits for each fleet of the winning side.

xr_conflicts.effect: The Chaos Space Hulk is in the booklet. Its 'low orbit' entry here is a scenario win condition, not the booklet's low orbit table entry (s.41).

xr_conflicts.xr_text: Orbital Weapons Platform / Orbital Torpedo Launcher

author: Cypra Probatii; ed. Marcin 'MKG' Gerkowicz
title: Incident at Kravertus II
forces: Chaos: Event Horizon (Repulsive class grand cruiser, Ld8, special torpedoes, overload shield capacitors). Imperial: Arbitrum (Vengeance class grand cruiser, Ld8, adept trimsman, navigational shield), LCV-67 orbital station, and patrol groups Thames (2 Firestorms, 1 Sword) and Rhein (1 Firestorm, 2 Swords) as reinforcements.
summary: Historical 895.M34: the Event Horizon turns on the Arbitrum near Kravertus II (medium planet, no moons, one asteroid belt). The Chaos player places the Event Horizon by scatter dice and 4D6 from a chosen point. Reinforcement patrol groups arrive from turn 3 on a 4+. Victory is by a points sum from -1/-3/+1/+3/+3 events.
special_rules: No special orders except Brace for Impact in turn 1
Low supplies: orbital station launches only Fury interceptors, 2 squadrons
Disengaging: Imperial ships only into Kravertus II's low orbit; the Chaos vessel only by the assigned edge; other exits count as destroyed
Reinforcements on a 4+ from turn 3

xr_conflicts.source_text: Imperial ships may only disengage by moving into the low orbit of Kravertus II (there is no separate low orbit table - ships just disengage by hiding in the higher atmosphere). ... In any other case, ships are counted as being destroyed.
xr_conflicts.xr_text: any vessel that moves off of the table edge during play for any reason counts as being disengaged (whether it intended to or not)
xr_conflicts.effect: Replaces the XR disengage by Leadership test and table edge. Leaving by an unassigned edge counts as destroyed instead of disengaged.

xr_conflicts.source_text: To determine the winner, add the following points and compare it with the table.
xr_conflicts.xr_text: Victory points are earned as follows: Enemies Destroyed ... Enemies Crippled ...
xr_conflicts.effect: Replaces the VP system with a points sum (Event Horizon crippled -1, destroyed -3, escapes +3 ...). VP are not used.

xr_conflicts.source_text: adept trimsman; navigational shield
xr_conflicts.xr_text: Refits
xr_conflicts.effect: 'Navigational shield', 'adept trimsman' and 'overload shield capacitors' are not Appendix 2 refits by those names; each needs a ruling.

xr_conflicts.source_text: special torpedoes (roll D6 as normal)
xr_conflicts.xr_section: s.16 Torpedo Types; Chaos Anointed Munitions
xr_conflicts.xr_text: Torpedo Types
xr_conflicts.effect: Presumed Chaos 'Anointed Munitions'-style D3/D6 roll; the source gives no rule.

xr_conflicts: Checked: asteroid belt and outer reaches (s.39); first turn set by the scenario; Fury interceptors exist as Fury Fighters in the booklet.
missing_or_unclear: Event Horizon's 'Venerable' status and profile (the Repulsive grand cruiser is in the Chaos list).
Navigational shield, adept trimsman, overload capacitors.
Where the Chaos player may choose the Event Horizon's deployment point within 20cm of the Arbitrum (the diagram).
Orbital station LCV-67 profile.
Heading of the reinforcements.
notes: Two-ship duel with reinforcements; a small-game. Re-fight forces on the following page.

author: Cypra Probatii; ed. Marcin 'MKG' Gerkowicz
title: The Fall of Great Armada
forces: Chaos 1500 points plus 8 free Fireships. Imperial 2500 points. Historical re-fight: Warhost Nemesis list with Sir Francis Gherkov aboard the Blasphemer class Revenge; Imperial Admiral Sedina Nidonia (Ld9, 1 extra re-roll) aboard an Apocalypse battleship.
summary: An Imperial fleet loading regiments is attacked by Chaos fireships. Imperial forces start on stand-by except D3 escort squadrons or light cruisers. VP as normal plus 50% (10% if crippled) of the ship's value for every Imperial vessel that leaves by the Chaos table edge. Eight turns.
special_rules: Fireships (free)
Imperial on stand-by
Imperial cannot use special orders for D3 turns and has -1 Ld in turn 1
Fireships deploy D6x10cm closer
xr_dependencies: Book of Nemesis: Warhost Nemesis fleet list (pp.26-27)

xr_conflicts.source_text: The Chaos forces have 1500 points and 8 free Fireships at their disposal.
xr_conflicts.xr_text: Chaos fleet list
xr_conflicts.effect: Fireships are not in the booklet; the source gives no profile in this scenario.

xr_conflicts.topic: VP for ships leaving by the Chaos edge
xr_conflicts.source_text: the player gains a number of points equal to 50% (10% if crippled) of the ship's value for every Imperial vessel which leaves the table by the Chaos table edge.
xr_conflicts.xr_text: Each non-crippled capital ship ... that has disengaged before the end of the game awards the opposing player ... 10%
xr_conflicts.effect: Replaces the 10% disengage value for that edge with 50% (10% crippled).

xr_conflicts.source_text: Imperial forces cannot go on Special Orders in the first D3 turns, and have a -1 Ld modifier for activating ships in the first turn.
xr_conflicts.xr_text: the defender at -1 Ld for the first D6 game turns
xr_conflicts.effect: Similar to XR's Raiders and Surprise Attack timings (D3 turns). Compatible; 'activating ships' is read as command checks.

xr_conflicts: Checked: deployment, first turn, game length.
missing_or_unclear: Fireship profile and rules.
Ld of Warhost Nemesis ships (list-dependent).
Who is the attacker (Chaos moves first).
Admiral rules ('profile and points cost of an Imperial Admiral' in the booklet is a Vice Admiral or Fleet Admiral).
notes: Needs the Warhost Nemesis fleet list for the re-fight but runs with any Chaos fleet.

author: Cypra Probatii; ed. Marcin 'MKG' Gerkowicz
factions_required: Tau (with Ambassador class Fynd'yon) vs Eldar
title: The Longest Travel
forces: Tau 1200 points including the Ambassador battleship Fynd'yon (use an Explorer with Additional Shield Generator and a random refit, or the Custodian). Eldar 700 points, up to 200 points of Imperial or Chaos escorts.
summary: A convoy variant. The Eldar place face-down contact markers (one per capital ship or squadron plus D6 dummies, 30cm apart, 30cm from the edges). The Tau enter from a random short edge, 45cm from the long edges. A marker activates when a Tau vessel comes within 30cm. The Tau win if Fynd'yon exits uncrippled by the far short edge.
special_rules: Contact markers
Eldar may activate one marker voluntarily each turn (two if Tau use special orders)
Eldar victories: marginal if Fynd'yon exits crippled, total if destroyed

xr_conflicts.xr_text: the booklet uses the fan Eldar MMS v2.0 rules, which take priority over XR's Eldar
xr_conflicts.effect: Written for the older Eldar (Armada-era profiles and movement). Any Eldar fleet here plays under MMS v2.0 in the booklet.

xr_conflicts.source_text: The Eldar's face down counters are activated by a Tau vessel moving within 30cm of them.
xr_conflicts.xr_text: contact markers
xr_conflicts.effect: Close to the narrative Convoy's contact markers; reading is consistent, but the source does not give the activated deployment table (see missing).

xr_conflicts: Checked: terrain by Deep Space generator (s.39); first turn Tau; victory by the Fynd'yon leaving.
missing_or_unclear: Ambassador battleship profile (the source says no rules exist).
What each activated marker deploys and where.
Whether a deployed attacker is placed facing any way.
Whether human pirate escorts for the Eldar are legal under the booklet's Eldar list.
notes: Convoy Run variant with a single VIP ship.

The Booty (lost when its carrier is boarded or destroyed)

xr_conflicts.effect: The source lets either side board the hulk; under XR a friendly hulk cannot be boarded, and the hulk here belongs to neither side. 'Hulk' is used loosely for a derelict.

xr_conflicts.source_text: Then you must disengage with this ship. ... You gain a extra 500VP points if you manage to escape with the booty.
xr_conflicts.xr_text: a ship or escort squadron may take a leadership test at the end of its movement phase

Attackers choose between two terrain rolls

author: Cypra Probatii; ed. Marcin 'MKG' Gerkowicz
title: Gunnery Practice
forces: One cruiser with the lowest Ld possible in the fleet; a player's own asteroids.
summary: A solo exercise on a 120 x 120cm table. Each turn 2D6 asteroids enter from a chosen edge (10 entry zones, D10), move 4D6cm each turn and have 1-6 hits (D6). The cruiser must avoid them as in an asteroid field at -1 Ld and shoot them (Armour 6, D3 blast markers when destroyed). It wins if it survives six turns undamaged and destroys at least one asteroid.
special_rules: Moving asteroid targets
-1 Ld to avoid asteroids
Renown penalties if played in a campaign

xr_conflicts.source_text: If an asteroid passes your ship, you must avoid it as in a normal asteroid field, but you suffer a -1 to Ld due to the speed of the stone!
xr_conflicts.xr_text: ships moving through an asteroid field, or coming into base contact with the edge of one, must first pass a leadership test to navigate it successfully. ... A ship that fails this test suffers D6 damage
xr_conflicts.effect: Consistent with XR; the -1 is a scenario modifier. Moving asteroids are not XR asteroid fields.

xr_conflicts.source_text: Asteroids have an armour value of 6 and of course no turrets or shields. Place D3 blast markers when you destroy an asteroid.
xr_conflicts.xr_text: For each hit inflicted, place a blast marker in contact with the edge of the field
xr_conflicts.effect: XR shoots at fields as ordnance and needs a Leadership test; the source targets individual asteroids with Armour 6.

xr_conflicts: Checked: no celestial phenomena; one-player exercise; renown loss is campaign-only.
missing_or_unclear: Asteroid base size.
Whether Lock On or other special orders are allowed (not restricted).
Cruiser class (any with the lowest Ld).
notes: Solo game; for green crews in a campaign.
